body_html:
Knowing what to say at the airport in Spanish takes a lot of stress out of travel. Airports are full of fixed questions and announcements: the check-in agent asks about your bags, security asks you to remove your laptop, the gate announces a delay, and immigration asks why you are visiting. Once you know the phrases for each step, you can answer calmly and understand what is happening around you, whether you are flying into Cancún, Mexico City or Madrid.

Quick answer
  • Check-in: ¿Cuántas maletas va a documentar?
  • Security: Saque la computadora de la mochila, por favor.
  • Gate: El vuelo está retrasado. ¿Cuál es la puerta de embarque?
  • Immigration: Vengo de vacaciones. Me quedo diez días.
{{toc}}

Check-in and baggage at the airport in Spanish

SpanishEnglish
Vengo a documentar.I’m here to check in. (Mexico; Spain: facturar)
¿Cuántas maletas va a documentar?How many bags are you checking?
Solo traigo equipaje de mano.I only have carry-on luggage.
¿Me da un asiento de pasillo?Could I have an aisle seat?
¿Me da un asiento de ventanilla?Could I have a window seat?
Su maleta excede el peso.Your bag is overweight.
Aquí tiene su pase de abordar.Here is your boarding pass. (Spain: tarjeta de embarque)

Mexico and Spain use different verbs here: Mexicans documentan their bags, Spaniards facturan them. Both will understand either one.

Security

  • Coloque sus pertenencias en la bandeja. Put your belongings in the tray.
  • Saque los líquidos y la computadora. Take out liquids and your laptop.
  • Quítese el cinturón y los zapatos. Take off your belt and shoes.
  • Pase, por favor. Go ahead, please.
  • Necesitamos revisar su mochila. We need to check your backpack.

Security staff speak quickly and in commands. Listen for the verbs saque (take out), quítese (take off) and coloque (put).

{{image:2}}

At the gate and on board

SpanishEnglish
¿Cuál es la puerta de embarque?Which gate is it?
El vuelo está retrasado.The flight is delayed.
El vuelo fue cancelado.The flight was canceled.
Ya están abordando.They are already boarding.
Última llamada para el vuelo…Last call for flight…
¿Me permite pasar?May I get by?
¿Me puede ayudar con la maleta?Could you help me with my bag?

If your flight is delayed or canceled, these help at the desk: ¿A qué hora sale el siguiente vuelo? (When is the next flight?) ¿Me pueden cambiar a otro vuelo? (Can you move me to another flight?) Perdí mi conexión. (I missed my connection.)

Immigration

Immigration officers ask short questions and expect short answers:

  • ¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje? What is the purpose of your trip? — Vengo de vacaciones. Vengo por trabajo. Vengo a visitar a mi familia.
  • ¿Cuánto tiempo se va a quedar? How long are you staying? — Diez días. Dos semanas.
  • ¿Dónde se va a hospedar? Where are you staying? — En un hotel en Cancún. En casa de mis suegros.
  • ¿Me muestra su boleto de regreso? Can you show me your return ticket?

Entry rules change, so check them before you travel. For Mexico, the official source is the National Migration Institute (INM).

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Baggage claim and customs

SpanishEnglish
¿Dónde está la banda de equipaje?Where is the baggage carousel?
Mi maleta no llegó.My suitcase didn’t arrive.
Mi maleta está dañada.My suitcase is damaged.
¿Tiene algo que declarar?Do you have anything to declare?
No, nada que declarar.No, nothing to declare.
Son regalos para mi familia.They are gifts for my family.

In Mexican airports, you may have to press a button at customs that randomly lights up green (go ahead) or red (bag check). It is routine, not a sign of trouble.

A sample check-in conversation

Agente: Buenos días. ¿Me permite su pasaporte?
Good morning. May I see your passport?

Tú: Claro, aquí tiene.
Of course, here you are.

Agente: ¿Va a documentar equipaje?
Are you checking any bags?

Tú: Sí, una maleta. ¿Me podría dar un asiento de pasillo?
Yes, one suitcase. Could I have an aisle seat?

Agente: Con gusto. Su vuelo sale de la puerta doce. El abordaje empieza a las nueve y media.
Of course. Your flight leaves from gate twelve. Boarding starts at nine thirty.

{{image:3}}

Common mistakes

  • ¿Dónde está mi puerta? Understandable, but ¿Cuál es la puerta de embarque? or ¿De qué puerta sale el vuelo? is clearer.
  • Mi equipaje están perdidos. Equipaje is singular: Mi equipaje se perdió.
  • Joking at security or immigration. Keep answers short and serious.
  • Estoy embarazada by mistake. If you are embarrassed about being late, say Qué pena, llegué tarde. See {{link:embarrassing-spanish-mistakes|embarrassing Spanish mistakes}}.

For what to say if something goes seriously wrong, see {{link:emergency-phrases-in-spanish|emergency phrases in Spanish}}. Once you land, you will need {{link:taking-a-taxi-in-spanish|taking a taxi in Spanish}} and {{link:hotel-spanish-phrases|Spanish hotel phrases}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

Being comfortable at the airport in Spanish means knowing a few fixed questions and having your short answers ready. Practice the immigration answers out loud before you fly, learn the words for delays, and you will arrive calm and ready to use your Spanish. For more travel and everyday moments, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you say “check in” at the airport in Spanish?
faq.a: In Mexico, documentar; in Spain, facturar. For checking in at a hotel, use registrarse.

faq.q: What will immigration ask me in Spanish?
faq.a: Usually the purpose of your trip (¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje?), how long you are staying and where you are staying.

faq.q: How do I say my flight was canceled?
faq.a: Mi vuelo fue cancelado or Me cancelaron el vuelo.

faq.q: What is the green and red light at Mexican customs?
faq.a: A random inspection system. Green means you can go; red means your bags will be checked.
